examples.text: "Full name please." "Maurice Xavier Wu." "Where did you get the Xavier?" "My father was a missionary," he said.
examples.ref: 1976, Don DeLillo, Ratner's Star, Knopf, →ISBN, page 337:

examples.text: 'I keep telling you to call me Xavier,' he interjected silkily, aware that her reluctance to do so intrigued him. 'Xavier,' Laura agreed, and then hesitated. How could his name be so...so...enticing? Because it was foreign to her lips―lingering there like the juice of a fruit she had never tasted before? Or because it was impossible to say without first softening your voice?

glosses: A surname from Spanish [in turn from Basque], found chiefly among people of Spanish and Portuguese descent.
Any of various notable people with this name as given name or surname, especially Saint Francis Xavier, a Spanish Catholic saint and missionary (1506–1552).
A Ge language spoken by the Xavánte people in and surrounding eastern Mato Grosso, Brazil.
